**⚠️ Warning: Availability gate failed.**

- **Gate failed:** Availability at or above 99.5%
- **Measured:** 99.1%
- **Shortfall:** 0.4 percentage points below target

The incident-duration gate passed. The longest incident was 41 minutes, 19 minutes under the 60-minute limit.

---

## Weekly Availability Summary

| Metric | Value | Gate | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Measured availability | 99.1% | ≥ 99.5% | ❌ Failed (−0.4 pts) |
| Longest single incident | 41 min | ≤ 60 min | ✅ Passed (19 min headroom) |
| Number of incidents | 2 | n/a | n/a |
| Total incident duration | 53 min | n/a | n/a |

**Incidents**
1. 12 minutes
2. 41 minutes

**Overall:** The availability target was not met. Both incidents stayed within the duration limit, but the week fell short of the 99.5% threshold.

**Data note:** The figures don't fully agree. In a 7-day week (10,080 minutes), 99.1% availability means about 91 minutes of downtime. The two listed incidents add up to only 53 minutes, which would give about 99.47%. That is still below 99.5%, so the gate fails either way. Still, roughly 38 minutes of downtime aren't accounted for. They might come from unlisted incidents, degraded periods, maintenance windows, or a different measurement window. Reconcile this before the summary is shared.
